subject: Animation
title: Toei Animation: The Oldest Giant
description: A micro-lesson that makes Toei Animation: The Oldest Giant usable.

hook.text: Toei Animation opened in 1948 with a dream of becoming the Disney of the East.

buildup.text: The studio produced Japan's earliest animated feature films and trained generations of young artists.

discovery.text: Toei created Dragon Ball, Sailor Moon, and One Piece — some of the most popular anime franchises ever.

twist.text: A young Hayao Miyazaki worked at Toei early in his career before leaving to pursue his own vision.

climax.text: Toei remains one of the largest anime studios in the world, producing content for a global audience.

punchline.text: Japan's oldest studio still powers its biggest franchises.

quiz.question: What was Toei Animation's original ambition?
options: To become the Disney of the East, producing Japan's first animated features
To replace live-action cinema in Japan

details.summary: Toei Animation, founded in 1948, is Japan's oldest and one of its largest anime studios. Home to Dragon Ball, One Piece, and Sailor Moon, Toei has produced some of anime's most commercially successful and culturally significant franchises.
details.whyItMatters: Toei's longevity and catalog represent anime's entire history. From early feature films to modern streaming juggernauts, Toei's evolution mirrors the anime industry's own transformation over seven decades.
takeaways: Toei is Japan's oldest animation studio, founded in 1948
They produce Dragon Ball, One Piece, and Sailor Moon franchises
The studio's history spans anime's entire evolution as a medium

faq.question: What are Toei Animation's most important franchises?
faq.answer: Dragon Ball is one of the best-selling media franchises ever. One Piece is the best-selling manga. Sailor Moon defined magical girl anime. Pretty Cure continues as a profitable annual franchise. Together they represent billions in revenue.

faq.question: How has Toei adapted to the streaming era?
faq.answer: Toei launched Crunchyroll co-productions, started its own streaming service in Japan, and invested in global distribution. Their large back catalog provides steady streaming licensing income alongside new productions.
